headline: Recommended a health, safety and cleanliness standard for all city parks after discussing trash at Keach Park.
summary: Residents raised concerns about garbage and too few trash cans at Keach Park, compared with White Park. Parks and Recreation Director David Gill said daily emptying cannot continue, and a carry-in/carry-out policy is planned for all parks. Any changes would go through the budget by January, then to the Council in early May.
decisions: Approved the September 15, 2026 meeting minutes; the motion passed without dissent.
Recommended to City Council a health, safety and cleanliness standard for all parks; passed unanimously.
Requested acceptance of the 2027 website hosting; the motion passed.

decision_titles: Health, safety and cleanliness standard for all parks
plain_text:
Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, Justice and Belonging (DEIJB) Committee  
Meeting Minutes  
                                                      October 20, 2026  
City Council Chambers                                   
37 Green Street, Concord, NH 
                                 5:30 PM  
  
1. Call to Order. The meeting opened with a quorum at 6:10 p.m.   
  
2. Roll Call.  
  
Attending:   
• Zoey Murphy, Chair 
• Byron O. Champlin, Mayor 
• Jennifer Kretovic, Council Representative 
• Ali Sekou, Council Representative 
• Karen Juall 
• Noemi Hagen Wierwille 
• Sheila O. Zakre 
• Alison Murphy 
Absent:   
 
• Rev. Jean C. Beniste 
• Vijay Bhujel 
• Amy S. Girouard-Crush 
• Clement Nsenga Kigugu 
• Ghana Sharma 
• Usha Thapa Shrestha  
 Ex-Officio Member:   
• Cara Meeker, Representing Concord School District  
 
 
2. Approval of September 15, 2026 meeting minutes: Mayor Champlin motioned to approve the 
minutes. It was duly seconded. Changes to the minutes to include the formal names of people, and 
typo on page two to the word to ‘rationale.’ The motion passed without dissent. 
  
3. Meeting Overview.  
  
4. Council Referral regarding Trash Cans in City Parks, specifically the abundance of garbage and 
lack of trash cans in Keach Park, versus the availability of trash cans in White and other parks.  
 
Guests:  
• David Gill, Director of Parks and Recreation, City of Concord 
• Charm Emiko, Project S.T.O.R.Y 
• Ester Claudette, South End resident and Concord High Student 
• Christine Rioux, Concord resident  
 
DISCUSSION:  
 
David Gill, spoke about removing the trash cans in all of the parks. There have been times when trash 
cans have been removed and returned. In 2025, a fair number of the trash cans have been full of
household waste. Changes were made to remove the trash Mondays and Fridays but they were typically 
overflowing mid-week and it was not feasible to empty trash every day of the week.  
Spring and Summer the trash cans had been returned, but then taken back due to beer cans, household 
waste. Working with Overcomers Refugee Services, the addition of signs in multiple languages has 
helped encourage carry-in/carry-out. It isn’t perfect but it is much better. Carry-in/carry-out signs are 
also displayed on all City Hiking Trails.  
Why cans in some parks and not others: Decisions were made on usage. For Keach, the trashcans being 
emptied every day, due to the volume is not sustainable.  
The upcoming plans are to have a carry-in/carry-out policy at all parks. In 2019, there were two staff 
members at every park, to remove trash daily; typically 5,000 pounds of trash weekly for all 21 parks.  
Rolfe, Rollins and White Park each have two cans each. All are removed during winter.  
Changes would have to be presented in the budget by January timeframe and then to the Council for 
review in early May.  
Ester Claudette: Why is Keach the only park that has multiple language signs. Certainly, people live all 
over the city and are bilingual. It appears Keach Park has been highlighted, but persons of color live all 
over the city.  
David Gill: Agreed. RPAC is taking up the same conversation and it is valid. It should be posted for all 
parks.  
Ester Claudette: The signs should be more visible; they are too small to see.  
David Gill: Parks & Recreation installed two signs a cost of $40 each. Placement was where they 
thought there would be greater visibility for people. Larger signs would be most expensive but is a valid 
consideration.  
Councilor Sekou: When decisions have been made to move and change the trash pickup, did RPAC 
make this decision? Or was it City Council?  
David Gill: Advised to the board that his staff would not be able to continue the trash removal at the 
current pace needed as these are filled every day and cannot be emptied every day.   
Karen Juall:  The role of the DEIJB Committee is to look at equity; it is not the committee’s 
responsibility to determine the budgetary elements of this conversation.  
Ester Claudette: Equality versus Equity. This is not about everyone have an equal stake. It is about the 
need.  
David Gill: Secondary question regarded Port-a-Johns and there are two at Keach Park.  
Noemi Wierwille: Is the policy for carry-in/carry-out moving forward?  
David Gill: No. The three parks have all trash cans removed in November. Hoping this can be decided in 
the spring and resources applied to support these three parks in the conversation and the 18 other parks 
that do not have trash cans. Meanwhile some wards do not have a park at all.  
Councilor Sekou: Expressed appreciation for Mr. Gill mentioning the lack of a park in Ward 8.  
Noemi Wierwille: Carry-in/carry-out is not a workable solution for all users. Operational issues: is this 
managed by staff or is it managed by RPAC?
David Gill: As we are tasked to provide a service with our division, how can we do what we do with the 
vehicles and staff that we have? Can we use volunteers? Concord Critters Program works to remove 
trash along roadways over the summer. We can look at options.  
Ester Claudette: I see this as a community issue and not a staff issue.  
Councilor Sekou: The community makes these decisions through the budget process and staff carries out 
the council’s initiative.  
Mayor Champlin explained the last budget cycle and the funding challenges where 5 positions were 
removed during the budget cycle.  
Christine Rioux: Added her conversation regarding a large population of homeless people in the park. 
She spoke about picking up trash at the parks (about 2 hours) of time to clear the park). (Pictures were 
submitted to the committee) It is seemingly a lot of sports play on the fields. The view was vastly 
different at White Park where they didn’t have the same experience. Three trashcans together. No trash 
strewn about.  
Ester Claudette: As a past Camp Counselor at the summer program with Project S.T.O.R.Y, we learn 
when you are in an environment that is cared for, you feel cared for. Going over to the park in the 
morning when the park is littered in trash and seeing the way the kids see the trash, knowing they now 
need to be moved to play in the trees area because of the garbage, the kids are less excited and uncared 
for. This is negatively impacting the children. While it is not intentional, the end results are a cause of 
feeling neglected. (Ester is here to represent the voice of those kids.) 
David Gill: Very few permitted uses of the park – a lot of the activity was at night, as part of the 
education and get the word out that it is carry in / carry out.  
Councilor Sekou: The perception still exists in the community that our minority community is 
concentrated at Keach Park and sees the reality that our whole community has greater diversity than 
previous years. We need to take that stigma and perception out.  
David Gill: Perhaps we will go back to a community meeting at the park to talk with the people that use 
the parks.  
Noemi Wierwille: We all want to meet the minimum for safety and cleanliness should be what we aspire 
to do.  
 
RECOMMENDATIONS FROM THE DISCUSSION: 
Question posed: Should we recommend a standard for all our parks? Health, Safety, Cleanliness across 
all of our parks, and this is the recommendation we would make across all of our facilities.  
Mayor Champlin agreed, taking an approach that is a broader look and fairness and equity and not 
attention given to only one or two parks.  
Sheila Zakre: Suggested we make a policy that we propose a minimum standard for all parks.  
Noemi Wierwille suggested we determine what the need is, but the committee doesn’t make the decision. 
Focusing on health, safety and cleanliness.  
Karen Juall shared her frustration that we are not dealing with the issue presented to us, which is the 
trash at Keach Park not being addressed.
MOTION:  
Committee will make a recommendation back to City Council that we make/create and set a standard of 
health, safety and cleanliness across all parks. As a city, we should be holding a standard across all 
facilities. Motioned by Noemi Wierwille, and duly seconded. Passed unanimously.  
 
5. OTHER BUSINESS: 
• Sheila Zakre proposed the next meeting we talk specifically about DEIJB needs and the 
role of the committee. What do we as a group see as our role. And how can we be 
responsive to referrals that come before us.   
• Each year, Councilor Kretovic pays for the hosting of the concordnh-
oursharedprosperity.com. Motion to request acceptance of the website hosting for 2027 
made by Councilor Sekou and duly seconded. Motion passed. 
 
6. Meeting time and Next Meeting: November 17th at 5:30 p.m. Mayor Champlin will 
confirm with City Clerk on availability of the Council Chambers. 
  
7. Motion to adjourn was made by Mayor Champlin and duly seconded. The motion passed 
unanimously.   
  
8. Adjournment. At 7:40 p.m. the meeting closed.  
   
Minutes respectfully submitted by Councilor Jennifer Kretovic.
